concepts.def: A wave in which the oscillations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction of energy transfer. Ripples on a water surface are an example of a transverse wave.
A wave in which the oscillations are parallel to the direction of energy transfer. Longitudinal waves show areas of compression and rarefaction, and sound travelling through air is longitudinal.

The repeated back-and-forth or up-and-down movement of a particle of the medium about a fixed position as a wave passes. The direction of this oscillation compared with the direction the wave travels is what separates the two types of wave.
A region of a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are pushed closer together than normal, so the medium there is at a higher pressure.

A region of a longitudinal wave where the particles of the medium are spread further apart than normal, so the medium there is at a lower pressure. The particles are still present; a rarefaction is not an empty space.
A wave on a water surface. Each part of the surface moves up and down while the ripple travels outwards, which is what makes it a transverse wave.
A longitudinal wave in which the air is repeatedly pushed together and pulled apart, producing compressions and rarefactions that travel away from the source.
A wave moves energy from place to place while the water or air it passes through only oscillates about a fixed position and is not carried along with the wave.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the types of wave is correct?
options: A wave may be either transverse or longitudinal.
Every wave is transverse, as the diagrams show.
The type depends on how the wave gets drawn.
Water waves are the only transverse waves.
mcqs.explain: The specification states that waves may be either transverse or longitudinal, so both types exist.

mcqs.q: Ripples on a water surface are an example of a transverse wave. Why?
options: The water surface oscillates back and forth along the direction the ripple travels.
The water surface oscillates up and down, across the direction the ripple moves.
The water is carried forwards across the pond as every ripple passes it.
The ripple is always drawn as a curved line in the textbook diagrams.
mcqs.explain: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer, which is what the surface does.

mcqs.q: A sound wave travels through air. What is a rarefaction in this wave?
options: A region where the air particles are pushed together.
A region where the air particles move across the wave.
A region where the air particles are further apart.
A region of empty space with no air particles.
mcqs.explain: A rarefaction is where the particles of the medium are spread out, giving a lower pressure than normal.

mcqs.q: Which statement about a sound wave travelling through air is correct?
options: It is transverse, because it is displayed as a wavy trace.
It is longitudinal, so it must have a solid to travel through.
It is transverse, with crests and troughs of moving air.
It is longitudinal, with compressions and rarefactions.
mcqs.explain: Sound waves travelling through air are longitudinal, and longitudinal waves show areas of compression and rarefaction.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a longitudinal wave and a transverse wave?
options: A longitudinal wave carries the material of the medium along with it, while a transverse wave carries only the energy.
In a longitudinal wave the oscillations are parallel to the direction of travel, and in a transverse wave they are perpendicular to it.
In a longitudinal wave the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of travel, and in a transverse wave they are parallel.
A longitudinal wave is drawn as a row of straight lines, while a transverse wave is always drawn as a wavy curve.
mcqs.explain: This is the defining difference: the two types are separated by the direction of the oscillations relative to the direction of travel.

mcqs.q: One end of a long slinky is pushed and pulled repeatedly along its length. Which description of the wave produced is correct?
options: Longitudinal, because the coils vibrate along the direction the wave travels.
Transverse, because the coils vibrate across the direction that the wave travels.
Longitudinal, because the coils are carried along to the far end of it.
Transverse, because a moving bunch of coils is seen along the slinky.
mcqs.explain: Pushing and pulling along the slinky makes the coils oscillate parallel to the direction of energy transfer, giving compressions and rarefactions.

mcqs.q: A ball floats on a still pond while ripples pass beneath it. Which observation is evidence that the water itself does not travel?
options: The ball is carried away to the far bank by ripples.
The ball edges a little further forwards as each ripple passes.
The far side of the pond becomes deeper as the ripples arrive.
The ball bobs up and down but stays in the same place.
mcqs.explain: The float returns to its position after every ripple, showing that the wave passes through the water while the water stays put.

mcqs.q: A loudspeaker plays loud music. Which observation is evidence that the air itself does not travel across the room to the listener?
options: A steady breeze can be felt coming from the loudspeaker cone.
A candle flame placed in front of the loudspeaker is blown out.
No draught is felt by the listener as the music plays.
The music is heard a moment after the cone starts moving.
mcqs.explain: If air travelled across the room there would be a draught. The air only oscillates and passes the disturbance on.
